title: AI Code Workflow for Unity
author: Laffells
selftext:
Hey folks looking for some advice on a smooth pipeline for AI code implementation in Unity. 

Currently I'm manually copy/pasting code back and forth from ChatGPT to Unity. Results are good but workflow is cumbersome. AI chat context can get lost sometimes too.

Ideally I'd have something much more integrated with Unity / visual studio. I'm very experienced with the editor itself and I make all my own art so I'm exclusively looking for a code workflow.

How do you guys closely integrate AI code with Unity?

comments.author: TeneTelrei
comments.body: I'm using Claude Cowork for Unity. You just need to grant access to the Unity project folder, so Claude can create script files directly. You'll have to set things in Unity still by yourself.

replies.author: Dismal-Scheme5728
replies.body: You want to be using Claude Code, not cowork. Just a different tab on the desktop app, or you can use the claude code cli in the terminal.

replies.author: Aesthetic-Engine
replies.body: What exactly is the downside of using cowork over code? Does it use more tokens or something? I've been using cowork exclusively for the past month so super interested to know.

comments.author: SmoggySPECTEREGaming
comments.body:
Use VScode within unity, and get the claude / codex plug-in.

Get the Get Shit Done powerfully off of github. It is a powerful agentic coding tool that can look at all your scripts and edit all your code simultaneously within the project itself.

I started with your same method, but shit gets real inconsistent real quick. The above method will save you weeks guaranteed. Godspeed fellow AI solo dev.

comments.author: TheBigDamAdventure
comments.body: I use web based Claude code and GitHub. Claude pulls my repo, adds his scripts to his own branch... then I test and iterate in his branch, and merge that branch into my main branch when it's in decent shape

comments.author: Emotional_Resort_207
comments.body:
you poor thing from 2024, get VSCode, get ChatGPT Codex plugin assuming you have the $20+ plan. init it once by telling it to "make me an AGENTS.md file with a one paragraph project summary, add the project hierarchy directories with filenames, for CS scripts add one liner summary for context, and add instructions to only read relevant files."
  


manually add any project-wide specific instructions, like "DO NOT list: don't use em dashes in comments" if those annoy you. it will remember and adhere to these instructions like 80% of the time. every day or whenever major changes are made tell it to update AGENTS.md with the new changes for better context awareness. keep it under 500 lines. 

  


then get coplay unity MCP on github and follow install instructions so it can read/write prefabs, objects, scenes, or even play test, etc. this will drain usage limits faster when MCP is on though. it needs to be turned on again if you close unity or the command window.
  


now it will have project-wide context always so it automatically knows which files to look at and which to edit.
  


give it elevated permissions so you don't need to manually approve every edit just have faith feel the vibes. give into the vibes. surrender yourself. no more coding. tell it to create a plan for X before switching to act and implement if it's a big ask like coding a state management system. tell it to implement the entire plan and have faith then go have lunch then come back to 10 scripts fully functional. it's also great at making editor scripts. 
  


other things to note, make sure to git commit often or if you are going full lazy vibes and dont mind wasting AI usage then add in AGENTS.md for it to git commit for you at the end of every implementation. start a fresh session in Codex whenever you start a new feature so the context doesn't bloat and rot. use your old ways whenever Codex usage limits is capped. now you are vibing.

comments.body: I have been using Bezi for a while, all the capabilities of Unity AI and Claude except no art generation. Great performance and smooth workflow!

comments.author: Cubey42
comments.body: Get Claude code and download the unity with AI, then you just configure the mcp server and Claude can work right in unity.

comments.author: jdshop
comments.body:
I use a coding agent (codex, cursor) plus a unity mcp . There are a few but I the one I am using is UnityMCP (OPEN SOURCE, not by Unity).

This way codex can do scene operations much cleaner without having to interpret the yaml files.
